children: Gold prices continue to trade in a tight range prospects of higher interest rates to curb persistent inflation weigh on the non-yielding asset. In early European trading, gold futures are down 0.1% to $4,372.40 a troy ounce. Meanwhile, the U.S. dollar index is up 0.1% to 100.71, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for overseas buyers. "The direction of the dollar and real yields therefore remains critical in determining whether geopolitical demand translates into sustained upside for gold," says Naeem Aslam from Zaye Capital Markets. Further losses, however, are capped by falling oil prices, which can reduce inflation pressure, and rising gold-backed ETF flows, according to analysts. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
